findings.summary: The scanner is a regex/token approximation of Java, not a parser; its refusal path is the only thing standing between a mis-lex and a silently under-counted TDD gate.
findings.failure_scenario: A future Java construct not in NOISE (e.g. a new literal form) lexes wrong, scan returns fewer methods than the counter expects, and the cross-check refuses rather than mis-reporting -- acceptable today, but the failure mode is a hard-blocked gate on legal code, so refusals must stay loud and diagnosable.

findings.summary: Several branches (the @interface branch, NOT_A_METHOD, the classes guard, UNICODE_ESC's even-backslash rule) are unconstrained by any fixture; the gap is now honestly documented but still open.
findings.failure_scenario: One of these branches is refactored incorrectly and every fixture stays green, so the TDD gate keeps counting tests that no longer exist.

findings.summary: The harness self-test suite is the only thing that validates the gate scripts, and it is not itself wired into a gate that must pass before the gate scripts change.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate script is edited without running check-harness-tests.sh; the pre-commit hooks still pass because they exercise the happy path only, and a weakened gate ships.
